newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar dips as U.S. Fed hikes rates.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar dips as U.S. Fed hikes rates.

text.p: Canada's dollar dipped slightly on Tuesday to C$1.3780 (US$0.7256) after the U.S. Federal Reserve announced a 25-basis-point hike in its short-term interest rate.
The dip is only minor compared to a two-percent drop in the Canadian currency's value against a strong U.S. dollar during the past month.
"The Fed move is fully priced into the Canada dollar," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed income analyst with MMS International.
With the prospects of an interest-rate-led surge in the U.S. dollar temporarily out of the way, traders said they were bullish on the Canada dollar.
"I like the Canada dollar against the crosses and against the U.S. dollar as well," said Nick Howell, chief dealer of foreign exchange with the Bank of Montreal.

"The Fed move could allow the markets to focus on Canada's strong economic fundamentals," said Palombi, who predicted the Canada dollar would trade in a short-term range of C$1.3690 (US$0.7304) and C$1.3730 (US$0.7283).
Traders said all eyes would now turn to Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen who is widely expected to hold Canadian interest rates steady.

Thiessen said last week that the central bank does not necessarily have to match any Fed rate hike, though he cautioned that his comments should not be interpreted as a pledge not to raise Canadian rates.
The reprieve for the Canada dollar, however, could be short-lived as the markets weigh the possibility of another Fed rate hike in May.
The prospect of a second tightening should cause a weakening of the Canada dollar past its 1996 low mark of C$1.3865 (US$0.7212), Palombi said.
